slides.title: Why Do We Measure? 📏
slides.text: Measurement is the process of finding out the size, amount, or degree of something using a standard unit! Without measurement, buying cloth, cooking, or checking a fever would be impossible guesswork!
slides.spoken: Measurement is the process of finding out the size, amount, or degree of something using a standard unit! Without measurement, buying cloth, cooking, or checking a fever would be guesswork!

slides.title: Numbers and Units! 🔢
slides.text: Every measurement needs TWO things — a number and a unit! Saying 'I want 2 of cloth' is meaningless. Saying 'I want 2 metres of cloth' tells the shopkeeper exactly how much to cut!
slides.spoken: Every measurement needs two things — a number and a unit! Saying 'I want 2 of cloth' is meaningless. Saying 'I want 2 metres of cloth' tells the shopkeeper exactly how much to cut!

slides.title: Four Physical Quantities! ⚖️
slides.text: At Class 4, we learn four common physical quantities: Length (metres/centimetres), Mass (kilograms/grams), Time (hours/minutes), and Temperature (degrees Celsius)! Each has a special instrument!
slides.spoken: At Class 4, we learn four common physical quantities: Length, Mass, Time, and Temperature! Each has a special instrument!

slides.title: Measuring Instruments! 🚰
slides.text: A ruler and tape measure length! A weighing machine measures mass! A thermometer measures temperature in degrees Celsius! A clock measures time in hours and minutes!
slides.spoken: A ruler and tape measure length! A weighing machine measures mass! A thermometer measures temperature! A clock measures time!

slides.title: Using Them Correctly! 🎯
slides.text: Always start a ruler at the zero mark, not the edge! Stand still on a weighing machine and wait for the needle to stop! Shake down a thermometer and keep it under your tongue for one minute!
slides.spoken: Always start a ruler at the zero mark, not the edge! Stand still on a weighing machine and wait for the needle to stop! Shake down a thermometer and keep it under your tongue for one minute!

challenges.question: Why do we need MEASUREMENT in daily life?
challenges.answer: To find the exact size, amount, or degree of something using a standard unit
options: To find the exact size, amount, or degree of something using a standard unit
To make things look pretty in the house
To waste time when shopping
challenges.hint: Think about buying cloth or potatoes! Without exact numbers and units, buying goods would be pure guesswork.
challenges.misconception: Measurement is not just for looks — it replaces guesswork with exactness so we can buy correct quantities of goods, cook properly, and check our health!

challenges.question: What TWO things does every measurement need?
options: A number and a unit
Only a number without any unit
Only a colour and a name
challenges.hint: Saying 'I want 2' is meaningless! You must say '2 metres' or '2 kilograms'.
challenges.misconception: A measurement is always a number PLUS a unit ('2 metres' or '1 kilogram'). A number alone like '2' tells the shopkeeper nothing!

challenges.question: When using a RULER to measure length, where do you place the zero mark?
challenges.answer: Exactly at one end of the object
options: Exactly at one end of the object
In the middle of the object
At the other end from the object
challenges.hint: The zero mark is the starting point! Placing the edge instead of zero makes the measurement wrong.
challenges.misconception: You must always place the ZERO mark exactly at one end of the object, because many rulers have a small blank strip before the zero!

challenges.question: Drag each step of using a ruler into the correct order!
challenges.hint: 1. Place zero at end -> 2. Lay ruler straight -> 3. Look at marking -> 4. Read to nearest cm
challenges.misconception: Using a ruler requires steps in order: first align the zero mark at one end, lay it straight, look at the other end marking, and read to the nearest centimetre!

easierVariant.hint: Take it slow. 1. Place zero at end -> 2. Lay ruler straight -> 3. Look at marking -> 4. Read to nearest cm

challenges.question: What does a THERMOMETER measure?
options: Temperature in degrees Celsius
Length in centimetres
Mass in kilograms
challenges.hint: A thermometer is used by doctors and mothers when a child feels warm or unwell.
challenges.misconception: A thermometer measures TEMPERATURE (how hot or cold something is) in degrees Celsius — it does NOT measure weight or length!

options: Length in centimetres
Temperature in degrees Celsius
